description: YOLO object-detection pipeline that detects cosmetic and optical defects on used cameras and lenses, then maps detected defects to a marketplace-style condition grade (Like New → Heavily Used). Adapted from an industrial bottle quality-control scaffold.
status: SCAFFOLD — taxonomy, config, grading logic and docs defined; dataset not yet collected and model not yet trained.

dataset.name: Camera & Lens Cosmetic Defect Dataset
dataset.source: TBD — to be captured (controlled lighting, raking light for optical defects)

grading.note: Illustrative cosmetic/optical rubric only. Not an official marketplace standard. Does not cover functional/mechanical checks (shutter count, AF, aperture, contacts).

limitations: Cosmetic/optical defects only — anything not visible in a photograph (shutter count, autofocus accuracy, electronic faults) is out of scope
Optical defects (fungus, haze, coating marks) are lighting-dependent and need raking/transmitted light to image reliably
Grading rubric is illustrative and must be calibrated against real graded inventory before any operational use
Defects are small and low-contrast relative to bottle defects — expect this to be a harder detection problem than the source bottle project
intended_use: Pre-screening / triage aid for cosmetic and optical condition assessment of used cameras and lenses. Decision-support for a human grader, not an autonomous grading authority.
attribution: Pipeline scaffold adapted from the Big Cola Bottle Quality Control project by Youssef El Demerdash (https://github.com/Demerdashh/bigcola-bottles-quality-control), MIT-licensed.
